name: ADR 0001 - Advisory agents never block merge
description: Both PR review agents post comments only; merge authority stays with the human.
content:
# ADR 0001 - Advisory agents never block merge

## Status
Accepted

## Context
Patrick runs two PR review agents in this landscape. NorthStarGuardian evaluates pull requests against a repo North Star and posts a structured interview. PRAgent comments on every PR with dependency/version/security triage and exactly five architecture alternatives. Both are designed to be useful, not authoritative.

The temptation with any review bot is to wire it into a required GitHub status check so PRs cannot merge until the agent is satisfied. Guardian already has the machinery to do this: a drift ledger, debt timers, and an `enable_blocking_escalation` flag. PRAgent's North Star states the agent must not edit files, commit, push, open PRs, or block merge, and advisory-only is enforced at six layers (token, tool allowlist, permission mode, PreToolUse hooks, output validator, and no write token in the agent environment).

If the agents block merge, every false positive or hallucinated finding halts delivery, and trust in the comments collapses.

## Decision
Advisory agents post comments only. They are not required status checks.

- Guardian's `enable_blocking_escalation` defaults to false. Drift and variance are recorded in the drift ledger and debt timers, but they never become hard merge blocks unless an operator explicitly opts in per repo.
- PRAgent has no repository write token. The synthesis agent is the only stage with PR-comment write permission, and deny_mutation hooks block any edit/write/commit/push/branch tool call.
- The human developer remains the merge authority in both systems.

## Consequences
- Humans retain merge authority; agents can be wrong without halting delivery.
- Drift and variance are made visible and routed (Guardian journal, sagas, Linear follow-ups) rather than enforced.
- Trust is built through comment quality over time, not through gates.
- A separate evaluator loop grades agent calibration and recurring failures instead of the merge button acting as the quality signal.
- Future merge-blocking is not forbidden, but it is an explicit, per-repo opt-in, never the default posture.

name: ADR 0002 - Transcripts are ground truth; repos hold distilled learnings
description: On-disk agent transcripts are the only complete record; agent-control-plane holds distilled learnings that promote to skills and ADRs.
content:
# ADR 0002 - Transcripts are ground truth; repos hold distilled learnings

## Status
Accepted

## Context
Patrick's coding work is done by Cursor, Codex, and Claude Code agents. Their session transcripts (Cursor agent-transcripts/*.jsonl, Codex rollout-*.jsonl, Claude *.jsonl) are the only complete record of what was actually said, attempted, and verified. A single coldaine-k8cluster rebuild in June 2026 produced 23 Codex rollouts, 7 Cursor transcripts, and 125 Claude jsonl mentions across 34 thematically dense sessions.

Two failure modes recur when this is mishandled:
1. Project repos become transcript dumps, burying product authority docs under session noise.
2. Agents answer from memory or from a stale PROGRESS doc instead of from live evidence, and the distilled learning is never captured anywhere reusable.

## Decision
Establish a strict authority order for agent learnings:

1. Transcripts on disk are ground truth for what was said and done.
2. agent-control-plane holds distilled learnings (sessions/, catalog/, promotion-queue/, capture/scratch/) with links back to transcript IDs. Learning IDs use LRN-YYYYMMDD-NNN.
3. frozenSkillz and ~/.agents/skills hold promoted, actionable procedures.
4. Project repos hold only facts about the product or system itself.

`/retrospective` writes session summaries to agent-control-plane/sessions/, never to project docs/history. Reusable procedures promote to frozenSkillz skills. Durable cluster or product facts promote to the project repo's ADRs or docs/history. The promotion queue lifecycle is pending -> resolved -> promoted.

## Consequences
- Project repos stay focused on product authority (NORTH_STAR, architecture, ADRs) and are not polluted by session retros.
- Learnings are searchable across projects via the catalog and referenced by stable LRN IDs.
- Promotion is explicit and auditable; nothing becomes a published skill without going through the queue.
- Transcripts remain the audit trail; the corpus is an index, not a replacement for re-reading the source.
- Agents that answer from a distilled doc without re-probing live state are caught by the verify-before-claim pattern, which itself is a promoted catalog entry.

name: ADR 0003 - Guardian memory is repo-native under .github/guardian
description: All Guardian-owned state is tracked repo content under .github/guardian; no hidden branches or detached checkouts.
content:
# ADR 0003 - Guardian memory is repo-native under .github/guardian

## Status
Accepted

## Context
Earlier Guardian designs stored review state on hidden Git branches or in detached checkouts. That made Guardian's memory invisible in a normal checkout, hard to audit, and easy to drift from the repo a human actually sees. It also created a second source of truth that competed with the human-facing North Star at docs/northstar.md.

A related risk: a pull request could modify docs/northstar.md and then be reviewed against its own modified rules, defeating the purpose of a policy check.

## Decision
All Guardian-owned state lives as tracked repository content under .github/guardian/:

- guardian-config.json (runtime configuration)
- northstar.md (Guardian active copy / snapshot)
- memory/northstar-snapshot.json (exact policy snapshot metadata)
- memory/amendment-log.md
- memory/journal/ (chronicle entries)
- memory/sagas/_index.json (saga assignments)
- memory/drift-ledger.json
- memory/debt-timers.json
- memory/dashboard.html

PR review reads docs/northstar.md from the PR base SHA via `git show`, so the policy used to evaluate a PR is pinned and immutable for that review. No separate storage branch, no detached checkout, no hidden local-only state.

## Consequences
- Guardian state is inspectable in a normal `git checkout` and reviewable in PRs, which makes drift and variance legible to humans.
- Every review is traceable to the exact policy snapshot (provider, document ID, URL, updater, fetch timestamp, SHA-256 hash) used for that review.
- The anti-pattern of reintroducing hidden storage branches or local-only state is explicitly rejected in the North Star.
- Cost: the repo sees churn from memory writes (journal entries, dashboard regenerations), which is accepted as the price of visibility.
- When Linear is the canonical policy surface, Guardian still materializes the fetched document into the active copy and records the snapshot, so the repo-native invariant holds even with an external policy source.
